newsitem.title: USA: Muni futures open interest nearly double year ago.
newsitem.headline: Muni futures open interest nearly double year ago.

text.p: While some may grumble about municipal bond futures contract illiquidity, open interest has increased dramatically in the past four or five months.
Chicago Board of Trade figures show open interest in municipal futures contracts on May 19 totaled 23,406, nearly double the 12,734 of open interest on May 20, 1996.

"In fact, the contract is far more liquid now than it has been in years, and I give the devil his due, that's probably due to Goldman Sachs and their tremendous plays in the options, which has dramatically increased the open interest," said one trader of the contract. "I mean, there's 23,000 contracts outstanding."
The open interest pickup is even more dramatic in muni futures options, which increased nearly 40-fold in one year.

"Goldman has taken a long position buying calls and selling puts where he has done a tremendous amount of business," the trader said. "The open interest in the options right now the last I looked was over 40,000, and that's where the interest is coming from."
Chicago Board of trade figures show open interest in options increased to 39,785 as of May 19 from just 1,250 on May 20, 1996. May 19 was not a 1996 trading day.
"A year ago, you couldn't even get a quote on those things, now there's 40,000," he said.
In addition to Goldman, participation by Merrill Lynch & Co and Chicago Corp have also helped to increase liquidity, the trader said.
A Merrill Lynch & Co spokesman declined comment.
Comment could not immediately be obtained from Goldman Sachs and Chicago Corp.
